items.title: 🤖 GPT-2’den GPT-6’ya Yapay Zekanın Evrimi: Cümle Tamamlamadan "Otonom İş Ortaklığına" Büyük Dönüşüm! 👇
items.summary:
🤖 GPT-2’den GPT-6’ya Yapay Zekanın Evrimi: Cümle Tamamlamadan "Otonom İş Ortaklığına" Büyük Dönüşüm! 👇
Birçoğumuz ChatGPT’yi günlük işler için kullanıyoruz ama arka planda dönen milyarlarca dolarlık teknolojik savaştan ve mimari değişimden haberdar değiliz. Paylaştığım infografik, yapay zekanın sadece 7 yılda nasıl "insan beyni" hızına ulaştığını net bir şekilde özetliyor.
İşte teknoloji tarihine yön veren o büyük kırılma noktaları:
🧠 2019 - GPT-2 (Sıfır Örnekli / Zero-Shot)
Her şey 1.5 Milyar parametreyle başladı. GPT-2’ye bir metin veriyordunuz ve o sadece istatistiksel olarak bir sonraki kelimeyi tahmin ediyordu. Henüz ortada bir "asistan" yoktu, sadece gelişmiş bir metin tamamlayıcı vardı.
🚀 2020 - GPT-3 (Az Örnekli / Few-Shot)
Parametre sayısı tam 175 Milyar'a fırladı! "Bağlam içi öğrenme" (In-context learning) hayatımıza girdi. Sisteme birkaç örnek verdiğinizde ne yapmak istediğinizi anlayıp harika çıktılar vermeye başladı. Yapay zekanın asıl miladı buydu.
👁️ 2023 - GPT-4 (Çok Modlu / Multimodal)
Sadece metin değil; fotoğrafları, grafikleri ve dökümanları da anlamaya başladı. RLHF (İnsan Geri Bildirimli İnce Ayar) ile sisteme "insani mantık" aşılandı. 8K-32K bağlam penceresiyle devasa dosyaları tek seferde okuyabilir hale geldi.
🧬 2025 - GPT-5 (Akıl Yürütme / Reasoning)
OpenAI’ın o meşhur "Düşünen Yapay Zeka" (o1/o3) devrimi. Sistem artık soruyu görür görmez refleks olarak cevap vermiyor; "Akıl Yürütme Jetonları" (Reasoning Tokens) harcayarak arka planda derinlemesine düşünüyor, strateji kuruyor ve hata payını sıfıra indiriyor. ChatGPT içerisindeki akıllı yönlendiriciler (router) sistemin beyni oldu.
🌐 2026 - GPT-6 (Asenkron ve Otonom Araçlar)
Ve bugün ulaştığımız son nokta... GPT-6 artık sadece bir sohbet botu değil; sizin yerinize arka planda saatlerce çalışan, kod yazan, analiz yapan "Asenkron Araçlar" kullanıyor. 1.05 Milyon bağlam penceresiyle koca bir kütüphaneyi hafızasında tutuyor, "tur ortası yönlendirme" ile konuşma esnasında kendi hatalarını anlık düzeltiyor ve tamamen aranabilir kişisel notlar tutuyor.
💡 ÖZETLE: Yapay zeka artık "cümle kuran bir çocuk" aşamasından, "sizin yerinize şirket yönetebilecek otonom bir iş ortağı" seviyesine ulaştı.
Sizce bu hızla gidersek önümüzdeki birkaç yıl içinde yapay zeka iş dünyasını nasıl şekillendirecek? Bilgileri kaybetmemek için yer işaretlerine eklemeyi unutmayın, yorumlarda tartışalım! 👇

items.title: GoodData.AI Launches the Agentic Serving Plane, a New Category of Enterprise Data Infrastructure for AI Agents - The Detroit News (JOA)
items.summary:
One governed layer serves data, semantics, context, and policy to dashboards, applications, assistants, and autonomous agents without requiring enterprises to rebuild the data foundation for every use case.

SAN FRANCISCO, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / GoodData.AI, the open agentic analytics platform, today launched the Agentic Serving Plane, a governed execution layer designed for the high-concurrency, context-rich data workloads created by AI agents. [...] Local Inference, planned to begin rolling out in the coming months, will allow selected AI capabilities to run closer to governed enterprise data without requiring a third-party model provider in the data path.

The architecture is designed to reduce latency and external inference cost while keeping AI execution closely aligned with customer-controlled business definitions, permissions and data context. [...] A person opens a dashboard and picks a filter. An agent keeps asking until the task is done, and its authority may need to be narrower than that of the person who initiated it. When a question cannot be answered within the available semantic, policy or data boundary, the system should say so rather than produce a plausible number.

Ondrej Macek, VP of Product, GoodData.AI

Stanek describes the strategy behind the Agentic Serving Plane in his blog post, Built for When the Agent Asks Next.

Đảng Dn chủ đã giành lại quyền kiểm soát cả hai viện Quốc hội trong cuộc bầu cử tuần trước. Các ứng viên đảng Dn chủ cũng chiến thắng trong các cuộc bầu cử thống đốc ở nhiều bang, trong đó có Texas, nơi có nhiều trung tm dữ liệu. [...] Một số nhà đầu tư lo ngại những chiến thắng này có thể dẫn đến việc siết chặt quy định đối với AI và các trung tm dữ liệu.  
   
Mối lo này đã gy ra làn sóng bán tháo cổ phiếu bán dẫn và các cổ phiếu khác liên quan đến AI. Hôm thứ Năm, chỉ số Nasdaq gồm nhiều cổ phiếu công nghệ ở New York giảm hơn 5%. Cổ phiếu công nghệ đã phần nào khôi phục vào ngày hôm sau nhưng các nhà đầu tư vẫn thận trọng. [...] Một số chuyên gia cho rằng các công ty trung tm dữ liệu mới nổi có thể gặp khó khăn về vốn nếu các quy định chặt chẽ hơn làm chậm tiến độ các dự án xy dựng mới. Các công ty này đã dựa vào khoản vay để mở rộng kinh doanh.  
   
Nguồn tin thị trường cho biết điều đó có nghĩa là cổ phiếu công nghệ có thể vẫn bất ổn trong thời gian trước mắt.

Our political world is corrupted to the core, and I have zero faith left. I was a die hard Democrat. All those I supported have chose a path of deceit. I can’t support them. 

I can’t support the other side. The third party is a horrible bet… 

Everything feels run by children who make endless excuses. 

No one hustles at the top. It is all grifting.

If the minds I love ever see this, understand all my suffering was for love. For truth. For honor.

items.title: this is f*cking smart, one question now audits an entire codebase
items.summary:
this is f*cking smart, one question now audits an entire codebase

Sam Altman (CEO of OpenAI) just said the quiet part out loud: "attackers already have these models. the only thing left to decide is who uses them first." then OpenAI quadrupled its top bug bounty to $172,000

the fastest defense I've found is a single question to Claude Code across 880,000 lines: "what can a stranger reach that they shouldn't?"

40 agents take that question to every entry point and follow it through the router, middleware, database queries and file storage

every finding links back to the exact line that allows it, with a working exploit against a local copy

the run found 19 holes in 9 hours. 4 critical. 52 paths it couldn't prove stayed marked for a human

give your repository to Claude Code, then ask:

"Answer one question for this codebase: what can a stranger reach that they shouldn't?

1. List every entry point: routes, API endpoints, file uploads, webhooks, background jobs and admin panels. Give each area its own agent and tell it which parts the others already cover

2. Follow untrusted input from each entry point to every place it's used: database queries, file paths, outgoing requests, templates. Note every check it passes and every check it skips

3. Prove each hole on a local copy with the smallest possible exploit. Log in as a normal user and a logged-out stranger and try both. Drop anything you can't reproduce

4. Rank what's left by impact: data exposure, account takeover, money movement. Write a patch and a test for each one, mark unproven paths for review and show me the diff before changing anything"

ask it on your login and checkout flows first. that's where the $172,000 bugs live

items.title: SoftBank shares jumped 13.9% in Tokyo today. Minutes after the close, it reported a $7.1 billion loss.
items.summary:
SoftBank shares jumped 13.9% in Tokyo today. Minutes after the close, it reported a $7.1 billion loss.

The stock went from ¥3,400 to ¥3,872. Then the July-September numbers came out: a net loss of ¥1.12 trillion. Analysts were expecting a ¥129 billion profit. It's SoftBank's first loss in almost two years, per Bloomberg.

The strange part is OpenAI. SoftBank's stake there is now worth $99.6 billion on paper. It has put in $64.6 billion, the last $10 billion in October. So the biggest bet looks fine. What hurt was everything around it: finance costs of ¥790.7 billion in six months, up 132%, and a $3.73 billion loss on equipment for US data-center projects.

In the video below, Bloomberg's Peter Elstrom in May. He calls OpenAI Masayoshi Son's "biggest bet ever," paid for partly by selling Nvidia stock and borrowing. People inside SoftBank worried he was "a little bit starstruck." And for all that money, Son doesn't have a seat on OpenAI's board.

My take: the OpenAI stake isn't the problem yet. It's a paper gain. The interest bill is real, and it's due every quarter, gain or no gain. Retail investors bought the legend this morning. The company reported the cost of funding it this afternoon.

Tomorrow Tokyo gets to price both.

Are the fans early again, or did they just buy the top of a $7 billion quarter?

items.title: GoodData.AI Launches the Agentic Serving Plane, a New Category of Enterprise Data Infrastructure for AI Agents - The Detroit News (JOA)
items.summary:
One governed layer serves data, semantics, context, and policy to dashboards, applications, assistants, and autonomous agents without requiring enterprises to rebuild the data foundation for every use case.

SAN FRANCISCO, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / GoodData.AI, the open agentic analytics platform, today launched the Agentic Serving Plane, a governed execution layer designed for the high-concurrency, context-rich data workloads created by AI agents. [...] Local Inference, planned to begin rolling out in the coming months, will allow selected AI capabilities to run closer to governed enterprise data without requiring a third-party model provider in the data path.

The architecture is designed to reduce latency and external inference cost while keeping AI execution closely aligned with customer-controlled business definitions, permissions and data context. [...] A person opens a dashboard and picks a filter. An agent keeps asking until the task is done, and its authority may need to be narrower than that of the person who initiated it. When a question cannot be answered within the available semantic, policy or data boundary, the system should say so rather than produce a plausible number.

Ondrej Macek, VP of Product, GoodData.AI

Stanek describes the strategy behind the Agentic Serving Plane in his blog post, Built for When the Agent Asks Next.

items.title: OpenAI’s Plan to Stop AI Data Centres Overloading the Grid | Energy Digital
items.summary:
A vocal section of the American electorate were seeking assurances that AI companies will not overload power grids, while many candidates ran on a ticket of holding hyperscalers to account.

Before a single vote was counted, though, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, had unveiled its ‘Grid Protectors Program’ – an initiative that will see its future computing campuses ease pressure on the grid. [...] “Data centres are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and our goal with every contract we sign under this framework is to deliver value for them,” she says

At OpenAI, the bigger picture is always in focus.

“With US data centre capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most,” the company says. [...] OpenAI is working to ensure its data centres can actually benefit grids, rather than overloading them. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty

## What is OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program?

The programme, which was announced on 2 November, commits the company to working with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for cutting the power use of its data centres at times of need.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI: 3 giant IPOs and only 1 has sold shares
items.summary:
OpenAI has little reason to hurry while private investors keep funding it, and it has closed $11 billion in new money. The company has also given its own reason to wait. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company," OpenAI said in a statement, as reportedby CNBC. Public buyers would also have to judge a trillion-dollar price without some basic facts about the business. Most of OpenAI's sales come from [...] The private valuation has climbed fast, and the figure public buyers will pay is still unsettled. Private investors valued OpenAI at $852 billion in late March, according to CNBC. Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, is aiming for a $1 trillion valuation in the listing, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by The Next Web. That target is lower than what private investors last paid, which means the debut may not be priced at the private peak. Whether public buyers match the latest round or [...] The verdict on Anthropic will come only after trading begins, when buyers without a business stake decide whether $78 a share was worth paying.

## OpenAI

Illustration: Quartz

OpenAI has not yet sold a single share to the public, but private investors already value it at $1.25 trillion, according to Reuters. That valuation puts its planned listing among the largest stock market debuts. Nobody yet knows how much stock OpenAI will sell or when, so the size of its debut remains unknown.
